blocks.text: Each RUN, COPY and ADD commits a layer; COPY is the explicit default, ADD adds URL fetching and implicit tar extraction, and WORKDIR sets (and creates) the working directory for later instructions.

blocks.code:
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates libpq5 \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

items: update + install in one RUN; a cached standalone `apt-get update` goes stale and later installs 404.
`--no-install-recommends` saves tens to hundreds of MB.
`--chown=10001:10001`: avoids a separate `RUN chown`, which duplicates every file into a new layer.
`--chmod=755`: executable scripts regardless of host bits.
`--from=<stage|image>`: copy from another stage or image.
`--link`: layer independent of previous layers (better rebase caching).
`COPY app/ /srv/` copies the contents of app into /srv; use `/srv/app/` to keep the directory.
Multiple sources need a destination ending in `/`.
WORKDIR creates dirs owned by root; `cd` in one RUN doesn't persist.

blocks.text: Q: "COPY vs ADD?" A: "Both copy from the build context; ADD can also fetch URLs and silently extracts local tar archives. Prefer COPY for predictable behavior and use ADD only when you want exactly those features."

items: Clean up in the same RUN.
COPY by default; ADD only deliberately.
